chapter: Bix, Trumbauer and the Goldkette sidemen
title: Frankie Trumbauer and the songs Crying All Day, Three Blind Mice and Krazy Kat
summary: Morehouse was close to Trumbauer and wrote songs with him, including Crying All Day as a follow-up to Singing the Blues.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. What about some of the others? I asked you about Bix. How about Frankie Trumbauer? What do you remember of him? Was he the same way? Was he very much like Bix?
You were very close with Frankie Trumbauer.
Yeah.
You and he used to write songs together.
Yeah.
You wrote several songs with him, didn't you?
Yes, several songs together. Like "Crying All Day."
Yeah, "Crying All Day."
Do you remember how that goes? "Crying All Day" goes?
(HUMS AND BEATS OUT MELODY) Oh I forget it.
Also you wrote "Three Blind Mice". Was that with Frankie Trumbauer.
Yeah. That would be (HUMS AND BEATS OUT MELODY)

That's great. Let me go back for a moment to "Crying All Day." That was a song that you wrote to follow up, as I understand it, the hit record "Singing the Blues." You had a hit record of "Singing the Blues". And you and Frankie Trumbauer needed a song to try to make another hit.
Yeah, yeah.
That's when you wrote "Crying All Day."
Yeah.
I'm not sure I'm right on this. Wasn't 'Crying All Day' based, didn't you base that on 'Singing the Blues' or...There was a connection.
I don't know. It should be here.
Yes, I know. I can't remember the details. Well maybe I'll find it. Okay. You wrote something else too with Frankie Trumbauer, There was another song. Do you remember that? 'Krazy Kat'
"Krazy Kat"
How did that go? Do you remember how that went? How does that go?
I don't know.
You don't remember that either.
It went something like what you whistle. (HUMS AND BEATS OUT "THREE BLIND MICE")
It went like that.
(HUMS AND BEATS OUT MELODY AGAIN)
"Singing the Blues", how did that go again. Do that again.
(HUMS MELODY)
That was the biggest record that Goldkett had.
(CONTINUES HUMMING AND BEATING OUT MELODY)
